mission.title: coredns: Panic in route53 plugin fails to release lock and stops responding.
mission.description: Panic in route53 plugin fails to release lock and stops responding.. This issue affects 8+ users.

steps.title: Identify coredns troubleshoot symptoms
steps.description:
Check for the issue in your coredns deployment:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n coredns -l app.kubernetes.io/name=coredns
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=coredns -n coredns --tail=100 | grep -i error
```
Look for error: `invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`

steps.title: Review coredns configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant coredns configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n coredns -l app.kubernetes.io/name=coredns
kubectl get configmap -n coredns -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=coredns
```
**What happened**:
We use the `route53` plugin with a basic config 
```
route53 <SOME_INTERNAL_DOMAIN>.:<SOME_HOSTED_ZONE> {
  fallthrough
}
```
This works well for _almost_ all requests.

steps.title: Apply the fix for Panic in route53 plugin fails to release lock and stops…
Confirm Panic in route53 plugin fails to release lock and… is resolved
steps.description:
Verify the fix by checking that the original error no longer occurs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=coredns -n coredns --tail=50 --since=5m
kubectl get events -n coredns --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm that `invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` no longer appears in logs.

resolution.summary: ServeDNS holds zMu.RLock() for the whole duration of zone.Lookup(ctx, state, qname). When a record is a CNAME pointing outside the configured zone, Lookup calls into Upstream.Lookup, which re-enters the plugin chain and can block on real network I/O.

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with coredns installed or the issue environment reproducible.
